title: A plain seal answers rung 4 as the reseal does and keeps the ladder
intention: cairn/devices/tester: `cairn test --seal <proof>` reads read_ladder(proof) before running and applies the same rung-4 check as reseal.py:331 (proof_sha256 moved -> refused unless a ruling/answered-question id is given, via the same ruling_refusal), and a seal that lands while a ladder is open carries that ladder forward instead of dropping it.
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. This ticket closes live trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/seal-door-crosses-rung-4-without-a-ruling.json, a measured fault that enters as a bug (skills/intent/SKILL.md: a bug enters as a ticket, not through /intent). traces_to: Law 8 (a proof whose assertions moved since its ladder opened is not sealed by a second door that forgot the ladder); Law 4.
how: cairn/devices/tester only. Factor reseal.py's rung-4 block (:328-341) into a function rung4_refusal(proof, ruling_id) -> str|None in reseal.py; call it from reseal (unchanged behaviour) and from the --seal path in cli.py (:126 region / wherever the seal record is built) before running; accept the same --ruling flag the reseal takes. Where the plain seal writes evidence, copy evidence.reseal_ladder from the standing record when the ladder is still open.
falsifier: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_plain_seal_answers_rung_four.py under PROVES {'2dd69b2ba087': {'1','2','3'}} on a scratch validation store: (1) with a ladder bounding hash A and the proof now hashing B, --seal without a ruling exits non-zero, runs nothing, writes no record; (2) with a resolvable answered question id it seals; (3) a --seal while a ladder is open and the hash unchanged leaves read_ladder() equal to before.
